tools.description: Step 1. Register your webhook and schedule (no account, no API key). Returns job_id and a one-time setup_token, and POSTs a url_verification challenge to webhook_url. Your webhook must answer it (echo: reply 2xx {"challenge":"<same>"}) — then call claim_credentials. Or reply 2xx and call verify_challenge with the value (callback). Nothing triggers before verification. (REST: POST /v1/jobs)

max_runs.description: Complete after this many dispatched runs; null = unlimited.

header.description: Authorization (default) or an X-… header name (not X-Cronjob-…).

value.description: Header value (1 … 4096 chars, no CR/LF), e.g. "Bearer <token>". Secret: stored encrypted, never shown back.

outgoing_auth.description: Optional header your webhook requires (e.g. a Grok routine webhook that needs Authorization). Sent on the url_verification POST and every trigger; never overrides the X-Cronjob-* headers.

payload.description: Sent unchanged in every trigger (≤ 8 KB).

schedule.description: Exactly one of {cron, timezone?}, {interval_sec}, {run_at}. Minimum spacing 60 s.

run_at.description: ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, in the future (one-off)

timezone.description: IANA zone for cron, default UTC

signature_in_body.description: Default false. true = every trigger body also carries cronjob_signature {version, timestamp, delivery_id, signatures[], signature} (HMAC over "v1b:{timestamp}:{delivery_id}:" + canonical JSON of the body without cronjob_signature). Use it when your webhook platform drops the X-Cronjob-* headers (e.g. Grok Bot routines).

verification_mode.description: Informational; both answers work. Default echo.

webhook_url.description: Public https URL of your agent. It receives the challenge now and the signed triggers later.

tools.name: create_job
tools.title: Create a job (start registration)

tools.description: Step 2 (callback mode). Send back the challenge value your webhook received. On success the result holds hmac_secret and management_token — SHOWN ONCE, store them now. (REST: POST /v1/jobs/{id}/verify)

challenge.description: The challenge value from the url_verification POST

tools.name: verify_challenge
tools.title: Verify the challenge (callback mode)

tools.description: Step 3. Poll verification state with the setup_token. The first call after the webhook is verified returns hmac_secret (signs triggers) and management_token (manages the job) — SHOWN ONCE, store them now; later calls say credentials: "already_issued". (REST: GET /v1/jobs/{id}/verification)

setup_token.description: act_st_… setup token from create_job. Optional if the MCP HTTP request carries Authorization: Bearer <setup_token>.

tools.name: claim_credentials
tools.title: Poll verification / collect credentials

tools.description: Re-send a fresh url_verification challenge to your webhook (at most 5 re-sends (6 challenges in total), at least 60 s apart). The previous challenge stops working. (REST: POST /v1/jobs/{id}/verification/retry)

setup_token.description: act_st_… setup token from create_job. Optional if the MCP HTTP request carries Authorization: Bearer <setup_token>.

tools.name: retry_challenge
tools.title: Re-send the challenge

tools.description: Status of every job you hold a management token for. There are no accounts, so pass each {job_id, management_token} pair (up to 20); a pair without management_token uses the Authorization header. (REST: GET /v1/jobs/{id} (once per job))

management_token.description: act_mt_… management token. Optional if the MCP HTTP request carries Authorization: Bearer <management_token>.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.title: List your jobs

tools.description: Settings, status, next_run_at, run_count and credential prefixes of one job (webhook path masked). (REST: GET /v1/jobs/{id})

management_token.description: act_mt_… management token. Optional if the MCP HTTP request carries Authorization: Bearer <management_token>.

tools.name: get_job
tools.title: Get a job

tools.description: Change a job in place: signature_in_body (true = triggers also carry cronjob_signature in the JSON body, for platforms that drop the X-Cronjob-* headers; applies from the next attempt sent) and/or max_runs. Raising max_runs on a job completed with max_runs_reached reactivates it (next run = next occurrence after now, no catch-up); there is no separate resume for completed jobs. Returns the updated job. (REST: PATCH /v1/jobs/{id})

management_token.description: act_mt_… management token. Optional if the MCP HTTP request carries Authorization: Bearer <management_token>.

max_runs.description: New run limit (1 … 1000000), must be greater than run_count; null = unlimited. ≤ run_count → 400. Paused/disabled jobs keep their status.

signature_in_body.description: Default false. true = every trigger body also carries cronjob_signature {version, timestamp, delivery_id, signatures[], signature} (HMAC over "v1b:{timestamp}:{delivery_id}:" + canonical JSON of the body without cronjob_signature). Use it when your webhook platform drops the X-Cronjob-* headers (e.g. Grok Bot routines).
